newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks finish at 4th straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks finish at 4th straight record close.

text.p: Mexican shares chalked up their fourth consecutive record close on Friday.
Analysts and dealers said shares gained on mild buying due to momentum gathered in recent sessions and market confidence Sunday's mid-term electoral process would be smooth.

"Basically no one wants to miss out on recent market euphoria," said Gerardo Copca, an equity analyst at the Finamex brokerage. "Some foreigners were buying today... They seem to expect the elections to go ahead without too many problems."
Final closing prices placed the blue chip IPC share index .MXX up 52.98 points, or 1.15 percent, at 4,644.60.
One floor trader said the IPC gained sharply for reasons that were unclear in the closing minutes.
"It looked like window-dressing on the home straight, it shot up in the last ten minutes on thin volume," he said.
Trading volume .TV.MX of 110.5 million was inflated by one single cross trade of 67.9 million shares.
Dealers said volume had thinned considerably due to U.S. markets having closed for the Independence Day holiday but U.S. investors were not entirely absent.
"Volume wasn't too bad, there were some U.S. investors in the market," a desk trader said.
"They call me from home with their orders and it's 48-hour settlement, so they pay on Tuesday. I feel foreign investors are no longer scared of the elections," he added.

Mexicans vote on Sunday for an new lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time, a mayor of Mexico City. Previously, that post has been filled by a presidential nominee.

The outcome of the mayoral race is critical, because for the first time President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) may lose control of the nerve center of Mexico to an opposition party.
The PRI has ruled Mexico for 68 unbroken years.

Analysts said they had nonetheless expected a PRI defeat in Mexico City for some weeks, and this was unlikely to affect investment flows. They said they would be more attentive to results for the lower chamber of Congress.
Dealers said market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) hauled the market, ending up 20 centavos to 19.90 pesos, a record close in peso terms.
Financial groups benefitted from recent falls in domestic and international interest rates, which could relieve their past-due loans burdens, traders said.
Spanish-Mexican financial firm BBV-Probursa gained 4 centavos to 2.25 pesos in relatively brisk trade.
BBV-Probursa and Telmex together accounted for some 16 percent of all shares traded, apart from cross trades.

Construction and cement stocks traded strongly, dealers said. Builders Grupo Tribasa ended up 80 centavos at 24.30 pesos on market expectations of a government plan to alleviate debts for highway concessionaires, they said.
Cement maker Cemex gained 30 centavos to 35.95 pesos on market optimism that a recovery in industrial output would boost second quarter earnings, dealers said.
The broad market mirrored blue chip performance, with gainers outpacing decliners by 69 to 17, out of 108 stocks that changed hands.
(( -- Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
